newsitem.title: UK: Britain slams Hong Kong legislature rights curbs.
newsitem.headline: Britain slams Hong Kong legislature rights curbs.

text.p: Britain on Saturday slammed new laws passed by Hong Kong's Beijing-appointed handover legislature which will curb political freedoms when the colony returns to Chinese control in two weeks.
The provisional legislature met in the Chinese city of Shenzhen earlier on Saturday and passed amendments to two Hong Kong laws governing the rights of assembly.
"We continue to regard these amendments to the Societies and Public Order Ordinances as entirely unjustified and unnecessary," a foreign office (ministry) spokesman said.
"They have already aroused concern both in Hong Kong and internationally."

The changes to the laws will empower police to ban protests on the grounds of "national security" or threats to China's territorial integrity and to disband organisations with overseas political funding.
The effect will be to curtail the rights of political parties and restrict protest marches.
Britain, which has held Hong Kong for the past 156 years, has said it will closely monitor China's rule of its former colony to ensure Beijing keeps to a 1984 agreement with London.
Under that agreement, China pledged that Hong Kong could keep its capitalist way of life and would enjoy autonomy in all but military and diplomatic matters after the handover at midnight on June 30.
But many of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people fear China will impose repressive communist-style rule, especially since the bloody 1989 anti-democracy crackdown in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
The amended laws will come into effect immediately after handover.
